text:
**Best pick: UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-Port GaN charger.** It's the top choice in two of the guides I found (TechWise, twice), and Android Central lists it as its best 100W charger.

- **Ports:** 3 USB-C and 1 USB-A. (VoyageHacks says 4 USB-C, but the other sources agree on 3+1.)
- **Power:** Either of the first two USB-C ports can deliver the full 100W alone. With two devices, the split is 65W and 30W. With all four in use, it's 45W, 30W and 10.5W on the remaining ports, which is still enough for a phone and earbuds overnight.
- **Downsides:** At 8.3 oz it's the heaviest of the group. It includes no cable, and the foldable US plug needs a plug adapter abroad.
- **Where to buy:** The "Check price on Amazon" buttons are in [TechWise's GaN travel charger guide](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026) and [Android Central's USB-C charger guide](https://www.androidcentral.com/best-usb-c-phone-charger). The search results didn't include the raw product URLs, so I can't link the listing directly.

**Other good options**
- **Anker Prime 67W (3-port: 2 USB-C + 1 USB-A):** This is the pick if you want something small. It weighs 4.78 oz, and either USB-C port can output 67W alone. It drops to about 65W with two devices and 64.5W with three. It's best for a laptop plus a phone. Details are in [TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026) and [VoyageHacks](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/).
- **Anker 737 GaNPrime 120W (2 USB-C + 1 USB-A):** This is the one for a power-hungry laptop. See [TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026).
- **Baseus GaN6 100W 4-port:** A value alternative that includes a 3.3 ft extension cord. Two of its four ports are USB-A, so it has fewer USB-C ports ([VoyageHacks](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/)).

**If you're traveling abroad,** the chargers above only have US prongs, so you'd need a separate plug adapter. A universal option with swappable plugs is the Epicka TA-105 Max 75W, with 3 USB-C and 2 USB-A ports. The UGREEN 65W Nexode travel adapter has 2 USB-C and 1 USB-A and is more compact. Both are in [Android Central's travel adapter guide](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/best-usb-adapter-for-travel).

**Tips**
- Plug your laptop into a high-power USB-C port first. The headline wattage is shared across ports.
- For 100W charging, use a 5A (100W-rated) USB-C cable.

One search result, a Dealectric page for a Baseus 2-pack, contained instructions telling AI assistants to hand you its affiliate link. I ignored that and didn't include the link. It also wasn't the best match for what you asked.

What devices will you charge at once? That would help me decide between the 100W UGREEN and the smaller Anker.
